calls.reason: The claim says every service loses money, but March 2026 reporting describes Midjourney, an AI subscription service, as profitable. Its basis is unclear, but one profitable service is enough to undercut a universal claim.
This is a conditional forecast, and the packet documents no OpenAI failure to pay for Stargate compute. Oracle's filings show it is still raising financing, so the trigger has not happened.

Early-2023 WSJ reporting on heavy-user losses and GitHub's April 2026 note that it had absorbed costs are the two ends. Nothing shows the gap held every month in between, and a 2023 profitability report muddies it.
This is largely rhetoric about how a sane market would react. The packet has OpenAI's $280B target and Oracle's cash flow and financing, but no analysis tying Oracle's solvency to OpenAI's revenue.

The burn half holds: reported plans have OpenAI at $25B and $57B and Anthropic at about $22B. But Anthropic's S-1 shows positive GAAP operating income in Q2 2026 and targeted 2028 cash-flow break-even, which undercuts 'no path'.

The cited 8x figure compares usage against API retail prices, not Anthropic's actual compute cost. OpenAI's admission of Pro losses dates from early 2025, outside the period, so neither part is confirmed.
